procedure: The teacher introduces the concept of systems using examples like cars and schools.
Contribute examples and ideas during the discussion.
Work in groups to identify and list the systems you interact with daily.
Choose a system and create a system map on a poster board, labeling its components and their interactions.
During a gallery walk, present your group’s system map.
Take part in the feedback session; listen to the teacher’s feedback and ask or answer questions.
aim: To understand systems and how different components interact within a system by creating and presenting a system map.

viva.question: What is a system?
viva.answer: A system is a set of interacting components that work together.

viva.question: Name one example of a system.
viva.answer: A school is an example of a system.

viva.question: What does a system map show?
viva.answer: It shows a system’s components and the interactions between them.

viva.question: Why are interactions included in a system map?
viva.answer: They show how the components affect or connect with one another.

viva.question: What is a gallery walk?
viva.answer: It is an activity in which groups view and present their work to one another.

diagram: Draw a system map of the group’s chosen system on a poster board; label the system, each component, and the arrows showing interactions between components.
title: System Mapping
precautions: Make sure each component in the map is clearly labelled.
Use arrows clearly to show interactions between components.
Keep the poster layout neat and easy to read.
Listen respectfully to other groups during presentations and feedback.
result: The group produced and presented a system map showing the components of its chosen system and their interactions.
